paper.title: Online learning with noisy side observations

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning with noisy side observations (weighted directed observation graphs)
unmapped: Weighted feedback graph with edge weights s_{t,(i,j)} in [0,1]; side observation c_{t,i} = s*l_{t,i} + (1-s)*xi_{t,i} mixes the loss with zero-mean independent noise bounded by R
Learner knows the noise bound R
Self-loop weights equal 1 (own loss observed without corruption)
Regret depends on the effective independence number alpha* = min_eps alpha(G(eps))/eps^2
settings.definition_quote:
In every round $t\in[T]$, the environment selects a weighted graph $G_t$ with $N$ nodes and a loss function $\loss_t:[N]a[0,1]$ ... the learner also observes $G_t$ and the feedback $c_{t,i} = \gweight_{t,(I_t,i)}\cdot \loss_{t,i} + (1-\gweight_{t,(I_t,i)})\cdot 
oise_{t,i}$ ... We assume that each $
oise_{t,i}$ is zero-mean, satisfies $|
oise_{t,i}|\le R$ for some known constant $R\ge 0$ ... we consider adaptive (or non-oblivious) environments

settings.name_in_paper: Online learning with noisy side observations (oblivious graph sequence, thresholded estimates)
unmapped: Weighted feedback graph with edge weights in [0,1]; side observations mix the loss with zero-mean independent noise bounded by R
Learner knows the noise bound R
Tuning of eta, gamma and thresholds eps_t may require knowledge of graph-dependent quantities
settings.definition_quote: consider an oblivious adversary that chooses the whole sequence of observations graphs deterministically before the first round.

symbols.R_noise: bound on the absolute value of the observation noise |xi_{t,i}| <= R
symbols.sum_alpha_star: sum over t of the effective independence numbers alpha*_t of the observation graphs G_t

conditions: noise zero-mean, independent, bounded by known R

source.label: thm:mainTheorem
source.quote: For all $t$, let $\alpha^*_t$ be the effective independence number of $G_t$. Then, setting $\eta_t = \sqrt{\frac{{\log N}}{{2(1+R+R^2)(N + \sum_{s=1}^{t-1}Q_s)}}}$ and $\gamma_t =R\eta_t$, the regret of \expwix is bounded as $R_T = \tOO\pa{(1+R)\sqrt{N+\sum_{t=1}^T \alpha^*_t}}$.

results.notes: Regret defined as max_i E[sum l_{t,I_t} - sum l_{t,i}] (max outside expectation), adaptive adversary; recorded as expected_regret. Paper's N = K. Proof gives R_T <= 2 sqrt(2(1+R+R^2)(N+sum Q_t) log N) with Q_t bounded via Lemma 2. Parameter-free w.r.t. T and alpha*.

symbols.sum_alpha_eps: sum over t of alpha(G_t(eps_t))/eps_t^2, where alpha(G_t(eps_t)) is the independence number of the graph thresholded at eps_t

conditions: observation graphs chosen obliviously before the first round (as in the proof)
tuning: constant eta and gamma optimized (exists a setting)

source.label: thm:naive
source.quote: For all $t$, let $\alpha^*_t$ be the effective independence number of $G_t$. Then, there exists a setting of $(\eta_t)$ and $(\gamma_t)$ for which the regret of \expixt is bounded as $R_T = \tOO\pa{(1+R)\sqrt{\sum_{t=1}^T \frac{\alpha(G_t(\varepsilon_t))}{\varepsilon_t^2}}}$.

results.notes: Existence of tuning; proof uses constant eta, gamma optimized, likely requiring T and graph sums; proof assumes oblivious graph sequence. With eps_t = argmin, becomes O~(sqrt(sum alpha*_t)).
